decision_summary: Town police hold a 24-month Flock Safety law-enforcement agreement ($33,000 total, $16,500/year recurring) covering 2 Flock LPR units and 7 Wing video integrations; town staff separately proposed a 7-site ALPR expansion funded in part by a $10,000 GOCCP grant. Signature and date fields on the agreement are blank placeholders, so no exact contract effective date is established.
notes: Product-mix details conflict across documents: the newer agreement lists 2 Falcon LPR units, 7 Wing video integrations, and 365-day extended retention for 19 units, while the staff report states 11 ALPR cameras are currently deployed and proposes 7 additional sites (expansion status unconfirmed). Cameras field uses the town's stated deployed count (11). Atlas 30-day retention figure predates the current agreement. Contract signature/date fields are blank.

decision_summary: No county procurement document or contract dates were located, but multiple independent sources indicate the department operates Flock Safety license plate readers: a Flock Safety case study describes the department using its LPR cameras in a retail crime-ring investigation, and a community document states the county already had 70 Flock Safety LPRs with data shared to the county police RTIC. Department headquarters is in Millersville per the county government site.
notes: No primary county contract or procurement record located despite targeted searching; this record rests on convergent lead evidence (vendor case study, community document quoting 70 Flock units, mapped cameras). Camera count conflicted (70 per community document vs 9 mapped by Finding Flock); left null. County is also known to operate non-Flock ALPR brands, so the newspaper article's ALPR references are not vendor-specific. Upgrade to high requires a county procurement or budget document.

decision_summary: On July 11, 2025, the Boonsboro police chief emailed council members a Flock Safety camera proposal with cost information; the July 14, 2025 council meeting agenda listed only a generic 'Police Department Report'. The Open Meetings Compliance Board found in September 2026 that the council violated the Open Meetings Act by failing to list the camera proposal on the agenda. A Flock camera was photographed in Boonsboro on July 16, 2026; the town scheduled a special meeting on license plate readers for October 5, 2026.
notes: Active status rests on a photograph of an installed Flock camera in Boonsboro dated July 16, 2026. No council vote, camera count, cost, or contract dates established; a special town meeting on license plate readers is scheduled for October 5, 2026, so this record should be re-checked after that date. Radio Free Hub City is a small independent Washington County outlet; its reporting quotes the official Open Meetings Compliance Board opinion and names the author as working from that opinion.
